status: REVIEW ONLY — nothing implemented, no option authorized
note: Options B and C are not alternatives: C is B plus a settlement target that is already implemented and usually null. They are compared separately because their failure modes differ where a governed criterion exists.

OPTION_A.name: PROMPT-ONLY CONTINUATION
OPTION_A.description: Further prompt engineering with no structural settlement representation. A v16 wording, or a different placement of the v15 rule.
advantages: cheapest by a wide margin; one file, no schema, no new surface
no new failure surface introduced, and nothing new to keep inactive
the §176/§178 static-proof harness already exists and would apply unchanged
failureModes: no measurement surface: the settlement decision stays inside prose, so the next failure is diagnosed the same way this one was — by reading raw output row by row

three prompt identities (v13, v14, v15) have now failed to move HR-04, and §179 replicate 3 reasoned explicitly through presence, the pre-start check AND the historical torque verification before settling the fact
each attempt costs a replicated hosted validation to evaluate; §179 cost 30 calls and $1.53991 to learn one row did not move
wording changes risk the precision half — §179 already shows 12/15 silence against a 13/15 floor
OPTION_A.determinismBoundary: unchanged — nothing deterministic is added or removed
OPTION_A.semanticBoundary: unchanged — everything stays semantic, which is the problem as well as the safety property
OPTION_A.legalSafetyTrustImplications: neutral to negative. The settlement decision remains unauditable, so a reviewer cannot show why a question was or was not asked.
OPTION_A.testability: static proofs only. §176 passed 30+ static proofs and changed nothing behaviourally; that precedent is the strongest argument against relying on this alone.
OPTION_A.compatibilityWithInactiveVerifierV3: total — it does not touch it
OPTION_A.riskOfOverQuestioning: MODERATE — recall-oriented wording has historically cost precision
OPTION_A.riskOfFalseSettlement: HIGH and UNOBSERVABLE — the failure mode is unchanged and still leaves no trace
OPTION_A.verdict: NOT REFUTED AS A CATEGORY — v15 was one wording at one placement, and PROMPT_ENGINEERING_CANNOT_SOLVE_SETTLEMENT is explicitly not established. But as the sole next step it repeats a loop that has failed three times and cannot report why.

OPTION_B.name: STRUCTURED MODEL DECLARATION
OPTION_B.description: The provider emits an explicit per-fact settlement declaration — evidence observed, what property it establishes, an assessment, an unresolved reason. The verifier performs STRUCTURAL checks only. No settlement target is required.
advantages: makes the settlement step representable, checkable and reviewable without making it deterministic
reuses an existing precedent exactly: a claim is treated like CHALLENGE_FACT_VALIDITY — settles:false, factStatusUnchanged:true — so it can never suppress a clarification on its own
gives the ledger's unreachable SETTLED_BY_EVIDENCE state a legitimate route (human review), and gives the unconsumed arbitration queue a consumer
independent of governed knowledge quality, so it degrades gracefully where acceptableEvidence is null — which is most facts today
turns HR-04's three prose summaries into three inspectable rows
failureModes: a fluent, wrong declaration is still fluent; structure makes it visible, not false
declaration burden may change model behaviour on unrelated axes — §167's movement was confounded by exactly this kind of bundled change
adds output tokens and latency per fact
without a target, 'what property does this establish' has nothing to be compared against except a human's own reading
OPTION_B.determinismBoundary: verbatim-span byte equality, one-declaration-per-supplied-fact, field presence, enum membership, the settled-and-bound contradiction, forbidden-field echo. All properties of FORM.
OPTION_B.semanticBoundary: whether evidenceEstablishes satisfies the owed property is never computed. CLARIFICATION_EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY = SEMANTIC_JUDGMENT_REQUIRED is preserved verbatim.
OPTION_B.implementationComplexity: MODERATE — one declaration block, a set of new admission codes, observability. All inside the already-gated stage.
OPTION_B.legalSafetyTrustImplications: positive. A reviewer can see what the system believed settled a fact and on what evidence. No new authority is granted to a provider.
OPTION_B.testability: HIGH — synthetic zero-call proofs can drive every structural check with known answers, in the style of the existing preflight suites.
OPTION_B.compatibilityWithInactiveVerifierV3: designed for it. The gate stays a literal false and no environment is consulted.
OPTION_B.riskOfOverQuestioning: LOW-MODERATE — asking the model to justify settlement could bias it toward declaring things unresolved. Must be measured, not assumed.
OPTION_B.riskOfFalseSettlement: REDUCED IN VISIBILITY, NOT IN OCCURRENCE — the model may still be wrong; it can no longer be wrong invisibly, and it cannot act on the claim.

OPTION_C.name: GOVERNED SETTLEMENT TARGET + STRUCTURED DECLARATION
OPTION_C.description: Option B, plus the owed fact carrying the settlement target the declaration is compared against. Per Q1 the target is acceptableEvidence.requirement — an existing field — not a new one.
advantages: everything in B, plus the comparison has two named sides instead of one
no schema change at all: acceptableEvidence is already typed, already provenance-governed, already projected to the provider with provenance stripped
insufficientExamples is already the §169 half — the evidence classes that look like settlement and are not — which is precisely HR-04's error class
the target is derived from an approved governed record through a hazard-agnostic sentence frame, so no one authors safety truth in this layer
failureModes: the target is null for most facts today, so on most facts C is exactly B

where the governed criterion is coarse it can mislead: §171 recorded that seven of nine distinct verification methods across twenty approved records are looking-based, the class §169 ruled insufficient
a coarse criterion could make a wrong settlement claim look supported, which is worse than no criterion unless provenance is carried into observability
invites pressure to strengthen governed records to make the architecture work — which would be authoring safety truth to fit a tool
OPTION_C.determinismBoundary: identical to B. Deriving the target is deterministic and byte-stable; comparing it to the declaration is not attempted.
OPTION_C.semanticBoundary: identical to B, with the target made explicit so a human reviewer compares two stated things rather than one stated thing and their own reading.
OPTION_C.implementationComplexity: MODERATE — B plus wiring an existing derivation into ledger construction
OPTION_C.legalSafetyTrustImplications: strongest of the options. The criterion is governed-sourced, its provenance is typed, forbidden provenances are refusable, and null is a legitimate answer.
OPTION_C.testability: HIGH — the derivation is already deterministic and total with five named refusal reasons
OPTION_C.riskOfFalseSettlement: LOWEST of the credible options where a criterion exists; equal to B where it does not
OPTION_C.verdict: JUSTIFIED — and it is B's natural second stage rather than a competing design

OPTION_D.name: DETERMINISTIC SEMANTIC SETTLEMENT GATE
OPTION_D.description: Compute settlement sufficiency deterministically — similarity, embedding score, keyword or property matching against acceptableEvidence.
whyRefused: it is the B_selectorAccuracy keyword scorer §160 and §161 retired, rebuilt in the production path rather than in a scorer
§160 established the failure concretely: the selector was satisfied by the observation text itself on 3 of 4 REQUIRED cases
it would convert a semantic judgement into deterministic truth, which is the one conversion the architecture is built to refuse
CLARIFICATION_EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY exists as a named constant specifically so this cannot be added quietly
OPTION_D.verdict: REFUSED — recorded so that a future reader sees it was considered and rejected on established grounds, not overlooked

OPTION_E.name: EXERCISE THE EXISTING ARCHITECTURE FIRST (A0)
OPTION_E.description: Before adding any representation, run the EXISTING owed-fact ledger, projection, declaration and binding machinery against the frozen §179 rows and observe whether the failures survive it.
OPTION_E.whyThisIsAnOption: Finding 4: HR-04, HR-05 and HR-07 all failed on the FIRST-PASS path, which has no ledger, no factKey and no binding. The architecture that would make a displaced question structurally refusable was not running. §179 is therefore not evidence against it.
advantages: zero new code and zero new schema; the machinery is pure and directly callable
cheapest experiment that could overturn the recommendation
if HR-04 survives it, the case for the settlement declaration rests on direct evidence rather than inference
if HR-04 does not survive it, the declaration may be unnecessary and the programme avoids building it
failureModes: local execution proves what the deterministic layer does, not what a hosted model does; a hosted step would still be needed and is separately authorized
constructing owed facts for the ten frozen rows is itself authoring, and must not become a route to re-authoring the frozen truth
OPTION_E.verdict: ADOPTED AS STAGE A0 of the recommended sequence rather than as a competing architecture

comparisonSummary.onDiagnosis: A leaves the failure invisible. B and C make it inspectable. That difference is the review's central argument, because §179 cost 30 calls to learn one row did not move and could not say why.
comparisonSummary.onSafety: no option grants a provider new authority. B and C explicitly deny it: a settlement claim is a request, and the fact stays UNRESOLVED.
comparisonSummary.onGovernedKnowledge: only C depends on it, and only where a criterion exists. Both B and C must fail transparently on null, which is why the governed-knowledge gap is parallel rather than prerequisite.
comparisonSummary.onCost: A is cheapest to build and most expensive to evaluate — every attempt needs a replicated hosted run. B/C are more expensive to build and cheaper to evaluate thereafter.
